cohort: 122 adult patients who underwent surgery at a hospital in the Southern Province, Rwanda, predominantly females (86.1%) aged 28-37 years (48.4%).
finding: The overall prevalence of Surgical Site Infection (SSI) was 8.2%, and being HIV positive significantly increased the risk for developing SSI.
mod_finding: Most (90%) of the patients who developed SSI had undergone Caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data was collected on patients who had undergone surgery, assessing SSI prevalence at an unspecified point or period post-surgery.
